title: Project ProtoStar links public research sharing to a climate AI challenge
dek: Hugging Face and research partners have launched ProtoStar to make scientific resources reusable, with a CMU climate challenge scheduled to test their practical value.

lede: Hugging Face and research partners announced Project ProtoStar on October 29 to improve reuse of publicly funded scientific datasets, models and code. A scheduled climate challenge will test those resources on a concrete research task.

body.text: The initiative targets practical obstacles to reuse, including missing documentation, unclear provenance, incomplete metadata and incompatible formats. Participating institutions commit to releasing suitable research artifacts through open infrastructure. The project describes those commitments as non-binding and non-exclusive, leaving institutions room to use domain-specific repositories as well as shared infrastructure.

Carnegie Mellon’s Climate Risk Intelligence challenge is scheduled for November 2–13 and uses historical weather records from 210 US cities. Organizers plan to compare predictions with statistical baselines and assess climate-adaptation ideas separately. The competition has yet to produce results.

claims.text: The October 29 announcement launches ProtoStar and schedules the first challenge to open November 2.
The launch blog and project page give different prediction-year ranges; participants need the final challenge rules.

buildersNote: Before preparing a November 2–13 challenge submission, confirm the final prediction period and evaluation rules on the challenge page.
